skill.name: agent-skill-trust-check
skill.description: Static security review for agent skill manifests, marketplace listings, MCP-linked bundles, and install instructions before local or external access.
skill.summary: Reviews agent skills before installation and reports risky trust-boundary signals.
skill.author: Tate Programs

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by scanner rules, security examples, Markdown code fences, and marketplace documentation. The confirmed risks are bounded local file reads and restricted GitHub/Gist fetches in the local CLI, plus an ambiguity between declared marketplace permissions and the packaged CLI behavior.

remediation.issue: Permission declarations do not clearly separate stdin mode from local CLI mode.
remediation.suggestion: State that the marketplace stdin runner has no filesystem or network access, while the npm CLI can read local paths and approved public URLs.

remediation.issue: The local CLI accepts local file paths from command-line input.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe path handling and recommend stdin mode for marketplace automation or untrusted agent calls.

remediation.issue: Packaged security fixtures contain dangerous example phrases that trigger scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep fixtures clearly labeled as test data and prevent agents from treating example content as operating instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Permission Boundary Ambiguity
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md declares network and filesystem permissions as false, while the packaged local CLI can read a supplied path or fetch approved public GitHub and Gist URLs. This appears intended, but marketplace users need a clearer split between stdin mode and local CLI mode.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The manifest lists no network or filesystem permissions, but the npm bin points to a CLI that supports local file reads and restricted remote fetches. The safer stdin runner is documented, so the issue is disclosure clarity rather than hidden malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Agent skill installs can expose local files, secrets, wallets, and external services. This skill performs a static pre-install review and returns practical risk findings.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SKILL.md text, marketplace descriptions, and install instructions for risky behavior signals.
Flags shell execution, destructive commands, secret access, wallet actions, network output, persistence, and prompt-boundary language.
Checks for provenance signals such as source, license, version, permissions, tests, and uninstall notes.
Returns an install-readiness verdict, risk score, findings, missing signals, and patch order.
Supports a stdin/stdout runner for marketplace workflows and a local CLI for files or approved public GitHub URLs.
limitations: It is a static text review and does not execute the target skill.
It does not prove dependency safety, runtime behavior, or sandbox isolation.
The local CLI can read local files and approved public GitHub or Gist URLs when used directly.
Pattern matches need human review because security examples and documentation can trigger findings.

use_cases.title: Screen a Marketplace Listing
use_cases.description: Review a submitted skill description before publication and identify permission, provenance, and prompt-boundary gaps.

use_cases.title: Check a Skill Before Install
use_cases.description: Run a quick static trust check before adding a third-party skill to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, or another agent.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Safer Submission
use_cases.description: Find missing safety documentation and risky wording before submitting a skill to a paid or public marketplace.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single SKILL.md file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SKILL.md text before installation. Report the verdict, main risks, missing trust signals, and the first fixes to make.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Listings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison for a buyer or maintainer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two skill listings for install risk. Explain which one has clearer permissions, safer behavior, and better provenance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Marketplace Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this marketplace draft as a seller. Return the changes needed to reduce rejection risk and clarify sensitive permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a High-Risk Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill for shell, file, secret, wallet, network, persistence, and prompt-boundary risks. Prioritize blockers and required guardrails.

output_examples.input: A reviewer submits a SKILL.md file that mentions shell commands, environment variables, and missing uninstall notes.
output: Main findings: shell access needs an allowlist, secret access needs disclosure, and uninstall steps are missing.
Patch order: document permissions, add guardrails, then add rollback notes.

output_examples.input: A creator submits marketplace copy with a clear source link, MIT license, tests, and no sensitive actions.
output_examples.output: Verdict: reasonable to trial in a sandbox. The report notes positive provenance signals and recommends adding uninstall notes.

output_examples.input: A buyer compares two skills where one sends summaries to a webhook and the other keeps output local.
output_examples.output: The local-only skill is safer. The webhook skill needs a destination allowlist, visible consent, and data redaction guidance.

best_practices: Review skill text before installation, purchase, or marketplace approval.
Treat findings as a triage report and verify risky lines in the source.
Use the stdin runner for marketplace automation with the narrowest permission boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean static report as proof of runtime safety.
Do not install a skill that asks to bypass higher-priority instructions.
Do not ignore missing source, license, version, permission, or uninstall details.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews skill text, SKILL.md files, marketplace listings, and install instructions for pre-install trust risks.

faq.question: Does it execute the target skill?
faq.answer: No. It performs a static text review and does not run the target skill.

faq.question: Can it review private code?
faq.answer: It can review text that you provide. The stdin runner does not fetch remote content or read local paths.

faq.question: Why can documentation trigger findings?
faq.answer: Security examples may contain risky terms. A human should verify whether the text is an example or real behavior.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should I do with a high-risk result?
faq.answer: Do not install until the author removes unsafe behavior or documents clear guardrails, permissions, and rollback steps.
